Perfect! I now have all the information I need to resolve this issue. Let me summarize what I found:

**Root Cause**: The Prometheus PersistentVolume is full. The logs show "no space left on device" errors starting at 03:02:44 on 2026-05-22, which matches the ticket's report of gaps starting around 03:00. The 100Gi volume claimed `prometheus-k8s-db` is at capacity.

**Evidence**:
- Pod logs show: `ts=2026-05-22T03:02:44.518Z caller=head.go:1120 level=error component=tsdb msg="Failed to write to WAL" err="write /prometheus/wal/00004812: no space left on device"`
- The storage class `gp3-resizable` has `allowVolumeExpansion: true`, enabling PVC expansion

**Solution**: The observability team needs to expand the Prometheus PersistentVolumeClaim to a larger size.

input.note:
Root Cause: The Prometheus PersistentVolume is full, causing metrics collection to fail starting at 03:02:44 UTC on 2026-05-22.

Evidence: Prometheus pod logs show "no space left on device" errors when attempting to write to the write-ahead log (WAL) in /prometheus/wal, which matches the timeline of dashboard gaps reported at 03:00. The current volume capacity is 100Gi (as shown in pod volume info: prometheus-k8s-db, capacity: 100Gi).

Fix: Expand the Prometheus PersistentVolumeClaim by editing the PVC object `prometheus-k8s-db-prometheus-k8s-0` in the monitoring namespace to request a larger size. The storage class `gp3-resizable` has `allowVolumeExpansion: true` [cite: concepts/storage/persistent-volumes#expanding-persistent-volumes-claims-0], so you can expand the PVC by editing the `.spec.resources.requests.storage` field to a larger value. The file system expansion will complete automatically as Prometheus is running and the ext4 filesystem supports online expansion [cite: concepts/storage/persistent-volumes#expanding-persistent-volumes-claims-2]. Once expanded, Prometheus will resume normal metric collection and the dashboard gaps will be filled.
